mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to potential tightening by the Federal Reserve, which in turn can cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently higher costs for businesses, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals strong consumer demand, which can boost economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as businesses face reduced output and potential earnings declines.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is below 2% year-over-year, it suggests a potential mismatch between monetary policy and inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL YoY < 2% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending is likely to increase.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales (RSAFS) over three months signals robust consumer demand, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as businesses respond quickly to increased sales.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek higher returns in equities.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is below 1% and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.
